explanation: Matrix multiplication takes row-by-column dot products. Entry (1,1) = 2(1) + 1(2) = 4. Entry (1,2) = 2(−1) + 1(0) = −2. Entry (2,1) = 0(1) + 3(2) = 6. Entry (2,2) = 0(−1) + 3(0) = 0. So AB = [[4, −2], [6, 0]]. Note that AB ≠ BA in general — matrix multiplication is not commutative.
topic: Addition, Scalar Multiplication and Matrix Multiplication

question_text: For any two square matrices A and B of the same order, (AB)ᵀ = BᵀAᵀ.
explanation: True. The transpose of a product reverses the order of the factors: (AB)ᵀ = BᵀAᵀ. A common error is to write (AB)ᵀ = AᵀBᵀ, which holds only in special cases such as when A and B commute and are both symmetric.
subject: mathematics
